newsitem.title: UK: Shaken LIFFE cocoa at 18-mth low as funds sell more.
newsitem.headline: Shaken LIFFE cocoa at 18-mth low as funds sell more.

text.p: Cocoa prices headed lower on Thursday, touching 18-month lows after a whacking sell-off on Wednesday which shattered the market's upside prospects.
Funds, put off by a gloomy picture on the charts, raided the market again with aggressive sales, driving May cocoa to 871 stg as they dumped long positions and increased shorts.
Origins were also selling, but traders said this was expected because of a stronger sterling against European currencies that increases exporters' margins.
"People are shaken. Last week this market looked as if it was going to go up, and in two days it's gone back down again," said one trader.
May was slightly off its lows at midday's 874 stg a tonne, down six, but technical analysts were looking for the July 1995 low of 850 stg to come under scrutiny.

"The attempt at recovery in cocoa was reversed with finality yesterday by the sharp fall," said Elli Gifford of Investment Research. "Some support may be found at around 800 but new targets can be set at 850 for the slightly longer term."
She recommended stops on shorts be put at 900 stg basis May.
A number of factors contributed to the reversal of cocoa's fortunes this week.
Traders said a continuous flow of cocoa offers by Ivorian shippers was keeping a lid on the gains, disappointing bulls who hoped for a full surge after last week's rise to 938.
Another disappointment was lack of industry demand as buyers sat on the fence.
But the final blow came from the latest weekly arrival figures in West Africa which suggested that, with no signs of a tail-off, the crop could be bigger than initial estimates.
"Ghana was the final straw," said one, referring to purchases of 15,614 tonnes in the week ending January 16 compared with 8,798 tonnes in the same period last year.
Turnover on the exchange was a robust 5,253 lots, mainly concentrated on the second-month May. On switches, Match/May traded back at 23 stg after close to 30 stg on Wednesday.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8072 march/may traded at 23 from close to 30 yesterday
